study_identification_part.si4_title: Structural brain abnormalities and aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia: Mega-analysis of data from 2095 patients and 2861 healthy controls via the ENIGMA consortium

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Quantify individual-level deviations in brain structure relative to healthy controls using normative modeling, and test whether these deviations are associated with concurrent aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia, including mediation by positive symptoms, impulse control, and illness insight.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Ordinal regression to associate deviation scores with aggression (ORs, 99% CIs); mediation analyses for positive symptoms (delusions, hallucinations, disorganised thinking), impulse control, and illness insight; sensitivity analyses adjusting for current antipsychotic dosage, duration of illness, and lifetime substance use disorder; additional analyses restricted to PANSS P7.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Greater aggression in schizophrenia is associated with lower total cortical volume and reduced global white matter integrity, with additional regional effects (DLPFC volume, IPL volume, internal capsule integrity); most effects are mediated by positive symptoms and reduced impulse control.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Aggression was associated with reductions in total cortical volume (OR [99% CI] = 0.88 [0.78, 0.98], p = .003) and global WM integrity (OR [99% CI] = 0.72 [0.59, 0.88], p = 3.50 × 10^-5), and additional reductions in DLPFC volume (OR = 0.85 [0.74, 0.97], p = .002), IPL volume (OR = 0.76 [0.66, 0.87], p = 2.20 × 10^-7), and internal capsule integrity (OR = 0.76 [0.63, 0.92], p = 2.90 × 10^-4). Except for IPL volume, associations were largely mediated by increased positive symptoms and reduced impulse control.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Individual-level normative modelling used at scale across 20 sites; authors suggest potential clinical utility for identifying neuroimaging markers to inform prediction and neuromodulation targets, while noting modest effects and the need for longitudinal designs and network analyses.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Cross-sectional design limits causal inference; aggression measured at a single time point and via single items may attenuate effects; potential confounding by measurement overlap in mediation; lack of information on comorbid ASPD/psychopathy; pairwise region analyses may miss network-level effects.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Multi-site ENIGMA-SZ dataset (20 sites). Methods mention normative modelling with z-scores versus healthy controls. Supplement Table S2 lists global IDPs used as predictors of local IDPs in the normative models. Specific QC procedures and site-effect handling are not described in the provided text.
